Yes, in your own name. You create it or we guide you, then add us as a user. We never take over your account. Any ad spend or marketplace fees are billed to you by the channel.

desc:
Google Shopping and marketplace product feeds carry your catalog to the channels where buyers compare products. Ecom Swift LLC prepares your product data, builds a feed that follows each channel's rules, connects it to your account and clears the errors we can see.

## What is a product feed?

A product feed is a structured file or connection that sends your product data to another service. Each product becomes a row with fields such as title, description, price, availability, image link, brand, identifier and category. Google Merchant Center reads a feed to show products in Shopping results, and marketplaces use their own feed formats to list items for sale.

The channel only sees what is in the feed. If a field is empty, wrong or badly formatted, the product can be disapproved or shown poorly. Approval and ranking are decided by the channel, so our job is to get your data as correct as possible before it goes in.

## Why feed quality matters more than the feed tool

Most store owners can connect a feed app in minutes. The trouble starts the next day, when the channel reports hundreds of warnings. Missing identifiers, prices that do not match the product page, images with text overlays and vague titles are common causes.

A shopper searching on Google sees a title, a price and an image, nothing more. A feed with a title such as "Blue shirt" competes poorly against one that says the brand, material, fit and color. The page behind the click may be excellent, but the feed decides whether anyone clicks.

## How feeds affect traffic and sales

A clean feed means more of your products are eligible to appear, and that they appear with details shoppers can trust. When the price and stock in the feed match the product page, buyers land where they expect and are less likely to leave. Accurate shipping and tax settings stop surprise costs at checkout.

Feeds also shape paid campaigns. Custom labels let you group products by margin, season or best sellers, so budgets can follow your plan. A broken feed wastes money, because ads may point at products that are out of stock or priced differently. Many factors outside our control influence results, including competition, the channel's policies and your pricing.

## What a healthy feed includes

- Titles that follow a clear pattern: brand, product type, key attribute, size or color.
- Descriptions in plain text with no promotional wording or shouting.
- Prices and availability that match the store.
- Product identifiers such as GTIN and MPN where they exist, and correct handling where they do not.
- Brand and condition fields filled in for every product.
- Product category mapped to the channel's own category list.
- Clean image links, with the main image on a plain background where the channel asks for it.
- Shipping and tax settings that match the store's real rules.
- Custom labels for grouping products in ad campaigns.
- A written checklist for keeping the feed healthy.

## How we prepare your feed

We begin by reviewing a sample of products against the rules of your chosen channel. We note what is missing and what can be fixed in the store versus in the feed rules.

Then we correct the data, build the feed or configure your feed app, and connect it to your Merchant Center or marketplace account. After the first fetch we read the error report and fix everything we can see. The Basic package covers one channel with common errors fixed. Standard covers two channels and a title format built for search, plus checks of identifiers, shipping and tax. Premium covers up to three channels, custom labels, two rounds of error fixes and a feed health checklist for handover.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Keep your store's price, stock and product page in sync with the feed.
- Use real brand names and identifiers from the manufacturer.
- Write titles that describe the product, not the offer.
- Re-check the feed after any large catalog change.

**Avoid:**
- Putting promotional text or capital letters in titles.
- Inventing barcodes to clear a warning.
- Sending products with broken or watermarked images.
- Ignoring warnings because the feed still loads.

## Who this service is for

It suits a store owner who wants to appear in Google Shopping for the first time. It suits a seller whose feed shows many disapproved products and who cannot work out why. It also suits a merchant adding a marketplace as a second channel who needs the data adapted to a new format.

## What we need from you

We need access to your store and, if you already have one, your Merchant Center or marketplace account, as a collaborator or user with the right permissions. We never need your password. If you do not have an account yet, we can tell you what to create. Please also send any supplier sheets that hold barcodes and brand names, since those details often live outside the store.
